label: copy-phase input h (fed-back h, from the 3rd original position onward)
explanation: Fires only during the copy phase, when the fed-back input token is the letter h. It is completely silent on h during the original phase, at the delimiter, and on every other input token. Within copy-phase h it rises with position: it never fires when h is the first original token being fed back (recall_idx 1), fires weakly and only about 40% of the time when h is the second (recall_idx 2, 4.7% of the mass), and fires at a steady ~3% per step from recall_idx 3 onward. The remaining false positives are mostly short sequences or the last copy steps, and some repeated h tokens. Output token, next output, first token and digit count barely change the rate. The top activations are copy-phase h at original positions 3-6 in long sequences.

issues: Reproduced test scores: P 0.918, R 0.886, F1 0.902, mass recall 0.953. Profile confirms zero activation in the original phase, at the delimiter, and on every in_tok except h. All activation mass is on copy-phase h with in_first==0.

recall_idx==2 (fed-back orig token 1) fires at a rate of 0.41 and holds 4.7% of the mass, as the explanation says. I tried splitting it by prev_tok (digit or vowel), in_count and L (precision 0.13-0.59). Nothing cleanly predicts which of these steps fire, so this is weak, partial firing and not a missed rule.

False positives (about 8%) are partly concentrated in L==4: precision there is 0.55 on 2372 predicted steps, and those steps all have to_go==0. Precision at to_go==0 is 0.85 against 0.95 at to_go>=2. Both match the stated 'short sequences / late copy steps' caveat. Excluding L==4 does not raise F1 (0.898 vs 0.902), so it is not worth carving out.

'Rises with position' is weakly supported. From recall_idx 3 onward the firing rate is flat (about 0.031), and mass per active step goes up only modestly from recall_idx 3 to 8. This is a minor overstatement, not a refutation.
I checked alternative predicates: t>=8 gives F1 0.83, to_go<=5 with recall_idx>=2 gives 0.89. Neither beats the original. No systematic counterexample class remains.
